properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 5:40PM MDT until August 30 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 540 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated earlier thunderstorms that
produced heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 0.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of slot canyons, normally
dry washes, creeks, streams and rivers. Hole- in-the-Rock
Road may be impassible in areas that receive heavy rain.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Croton Canyon, Coyote Gulch, Brimstone, Peekaboo, Forty Mile Gulch,
Fifty Mile Gulch, Davis Gulch and other drainages on
Hole-in-the-Rock Road.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The northwest side of the Turner Gulch Fire Scar burn scar in...
Southwestern Mesa County in west central Colorado...

* Until 800 PM MDT.

* At 558 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the northwest side of the Turner Gulch Fire Scar
Burn Scar. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 3 inches in 20 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the West Creek. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the northwest side of the
Turner Gulch Fire Scar Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
northwest side of the Turner Gulch Fire Scar Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southwestern Mesa County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Ute Creek, North Fork West Creek and West Creek.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the northwest side of the Turner Gulch Fire Scar Burn Scar. Severe
debris flows can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and
driveways may be washed away in places. If you encounter flood
waters...climb to safety.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 30 at 9:10AM CDT until August 31 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Illinois...

Wabash River at Riverton

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River at Riverton. The river
has crested. Flooding is expected come to an end on the Wabash later
tonight.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Some agricultural lands underwater.  A few
rural roads in Crawford County, Illinois close as water backs up
Minnow Slough.  High water affects campground at Leaverton Park in
Palestine.  A few private roads near the Gill Township levee in
Sullivan County may flood.  Water level is at the top of most
makeshift levees.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 AM CDT /9:00 AM EDT/ Sunday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 4.7 feet
Wednesday, September 09.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM CDT /1015 PM
EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 4:10PM MDT until August 30 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 410 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.25 inches of rain have
fallen across the northeast slopes of Magdalena Mountain. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Socorro County.

This includes Highway 60 between Mile Markers 121 and 128.
properties.instruction:
In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 930 PM MDT Sunday.

* At 228 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of normally dry washes,
slot canyons, streams, creeks and rivers.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bryce Canyon National Park, Buckskin Wash, Wire Pass, the Paria
River, Paria River Canyon, Bull Valley Gorge, and Willis Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 30 at 4:57PM MST until August 30 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 457 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 9 miles southeast of
Buckskin Mountain Park, or 11 miles southeast of Parker Dam, moving
northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
northern La Paz County.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 30 at 6:56PM CDT until August 30 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
The Severe Thunderstorm Warning that was previously in effect has
been reissued for Corson County and is in effect until 700 PM MDT.
Please refer to that bulletin for the latest severe weather
information. However, small hail and gusty winds are still possible
with these thunderstorms.

To report severe weather, contact your nearest law enforcement
agency. They will send your report to the National Weather Service
office.

A Severe Thunderstorm Watch remains in effect until 1000 PM MDT
Sunday for a portion of north central South Dakota.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 5:36PM MDT until August 30 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Northwest area of the Ferris Fire Scar burn scar in...
Northwestern Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 615 PM MDT.

* At 536 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Northwest area of the Ferris Fire Scar Burn
Scar. Between 0.3 and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen over 15
minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other
loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Northwest area of the
Ferris Fire Scar Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Northwest area of the Ferris Fire Scar Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Dolores County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Cross Canyon, Glade Canyon and Dolores River.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Northwest area of the Ferris Fire Scar Burn Scar. Severe
debris flows can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and
driveways may be washed away in places. If you encounter flood
waters...climb to safety.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Low water crossings in mountainous terrain can become dangerous in
heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate
route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become life
threatening in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams
or creeks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 30 at 6:55PM CDT until August 30 at 7:45PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
At 655 PM CDT /555 PM MDT/, severe thunderstorms were located along a
line from near Center to 19 miles south of Shields, or along a line
from 23 miles northwest of Mandan to 52 miles southwest of Linton,
moving east at 50 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile
homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Bismarck, Mandan, Linton, Lincoln, New Salem, Wilton, Center,
Strasburg, Carson, Hazelton, Flasher, Fort Yates, Selfridge,
Menoken, Sterling, Almont, Solen, Westfield, Cannon Ball and Regan.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. These storms have produced widespread
damaging winds.

NWSheadline: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 745 PM CDT /645 PM MDT/ FOR CENTRAL BURLEIGH, WESTERN EMMONS, EASTERN GRANT, MORTON, SOUTHERN OLIVER AND SIOUX COUNTIES

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 5:19PM MDT until August 30 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Grand County in east central Utah...

* Until 645 PM MDT.

* At 519 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moab and Castle Valley.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging currents in a matter
of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

UT-128 may be prone to rockslides and mudslides in heavy rain. Stay
alert for rocks and debris on roads, and avoid driving on flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Immediately climb to higher ground. Runoff concentrated through
narrow canyon walls can quickly become dangerous, life threatening
conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Tidal Potomac from Key Bridge to Indian Head MD
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 30 at 7:30PM EDT until August 30 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
SMWLWX

The National Weather Service in Sterling Virginia has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Tidal Potomac from Key Bridge to Indian Head MD...

* Until 900 PM EDT.

* At 729 PM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 14 nm northwest of Tidal Basin to 10 nm west of Key
Bridge to 14 nm northwest of Mason Neck State Park, moving east at
15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Boaters in small craft could be thrown overboard by
suddenly higher winds and waves capsizing their vessel.

* Locations impacted include...
Tidal Basin, Fort Washington, Reagan National Airport, Gunston
Hall, Woodrow Wilson Bridge, Key Bridge, Fort Hunt, National
Harbor, and Alexandria.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
